extraction_text: 敢死队在战场上向阿周那挑战，阿周那与敢死队展开激战。
德罗纳率领军队冲向坚战。般度族军队奋勇阻截德罗纳，许多武士为此阵亡。德罗纳多次发起进攻，没有获得成功。
难敌亲自率领象军，进攻怖军，也被怖军击溃。

extraction_text: 阿周那正在与敢死队交战，发现坚战这边遭到福授王进攻，情况危急。于是，他赶紧歼灭敢死队，前来援助坚战。
阿周那与福授王展开激战。福授王使出毗湿奴法宝，直刺阿周那胸膛。黑天挺身挡住飞来的法宝。
阿周那埋怨黑天没有恪守“只担任御者而不直接参战”的诺言。黑天告诉阿周那，这个毗湿奴法宝原本是他赐予阿修罗那罗迦的，又由那罗迦传给福授王。它能杀死任何人，如果不由他本人挡住，就会杀死阿周那。
然后，阿周那按照黑天的吩咐，用箭射死福授王的大象和福授王本人。
接着，阿周那大肆杀戮俱卢族军队。而德罗纳也大肆杀戮般度族军队。双方军队伤亡惨重。
难敌埋怨德罗纳没有兑现诺言，活捉坚战。德罗纳再次强调要在战斗中将阿周那引开。
于是，敢死队再次向阿周那挑战，引开阿周那。德罗纳排出车轮阵容，向阿周那发起强大攻势。
坚战委派阿周那之子激昂前去攻破德罗纳的阵容。激昂表示父亲阿周那只教给他破阵的方法，而没有教给他退出的方法。坚战表示只要他攻破敌人阵容，他们就会在后面一直跟随他，保护他。

attributes.relationship: 父子（阿周那与激昂），兄弟（坚战与阿周那）

extraction_text: 威武勇猛的激昂先后战胜难敌、难降和迦尔纳，闯入敌阵，坚战率领军队跟随在后。然而，胜车王率领军队冲上前来，截断了他们的去路。这样，激昂孤身一人，陷入敌军重围。
俱卢族德罗纳、慈悯、迦尔纳、马嘶、巨力和成铠六位大勇士围攻激昂一人。激昂浴血奋战。最后，德罗纳射断他的刀，迦尔纳射碎他的盾，难降用铁杵将他砸死。
双方军队收兵回营。阿周那在击败敢死队后，也返回营地。他得知激昂已经阵亡，直接原因是胜车王阻截住保护激昂的般度族军队。于是，他发誓在明天的战斗中一定要杀死胜车王，否则，他就跳入烈火中。
胜车王从俱卢族探子口中得知阿周那的誓言，十分恐惧，请求难敌允许他离开军队。难敌劝阻他，德罗纳也答应在战斗中保护他。
而黑天也从般度族探子口中得知德罗纳安排了保护胜车王的严密措施。为了保证阿周那明天取胜，黑天在夜里托梦给阿周那，带他一起凌空前往大神湿婆住地，求得“兽主法宝”。

attributes.supernatural: 托梦、凌空飞行、兽主法宝

extraction_text: Drona arranged the Kaurava army formation and placed Jayadratha in the safest position.
Arjuna fought fiercely to kill Jayadratha, defeating Duryodhana, Dushasana, and Drona's armies, and broke into the Kaurava formation.
Vriddhakshatra angrily threw the Varuna weapon at Krishna, but it rebounded and killed Vriddhakshatra himself because the weapon's rule forbids attacking non-combatants.
Arjuna killed King Shalya of Kamboja and many other Kaurava warriors who tried to intercept him.
Duryodhana complained to Drona about failing to stop Arjuna, but Drona explained he must fulfill his promise to capture Yudhishthira instead.
Drona personally put an invincible armor on Duryodhana, originally given by Shiva to Indra for defeating Vritra, to fight Arjuna confidently.
Arjuna reached Jayadratha, and Duryodhana arrived to engage Arjuna in fierce combat.
Yudhishthira, worried about Arjuna being outnumbered, sent Satyaki to support him.
Satyaki fought his way through enemies to reach Arjuna.
Yudhishthira sent Bhima to support Arjuna as the Pandava army suffered heavy attacks.
Bhima broke through Drona's interception, joined Satyaki and Arjuna, but was surrounded by Kaurava warriors led by Karna.
Bhima killed many of Dhritarashtra's sons but was defeated by Karna, who spared Bhima due to his promise to Kunti to only fight Arjuna to death.
Satyaki came to rescue Bhima but was intercepted by Bhurishrava, who knocked Satyaki down, grabbed his hair, and stepped on his chest.
Arjuna shot and severed Bhurishrava's raised arm to save Satyaki, citing his vow to protect allies within his range.
Bhurishrava accused Arjuna of violating combat rules by attacking someone not engaged with him, then sat fasting to death.
Satyaki, ignoring劝阻, beheaded the seated Bhurishrava.
As sunset approached, Krishna urged Arjuna to kill Jayadratha quickly, while Duryodhana urged Karna to intercept Arjuna until sunset to void Arjuna's vow.

attributes.stakes: Arjuna's vow of self-immolation if failed

extraction_text: Arjuna finally shot off Jayadratha's head after bloody combat.
The armies continued fighting past sunset into a brutal night battle with unclear outcome.
Karna's fierce fighting caused the Pandava army to flee, and Yudhishthira considered retreating.
Arjuna prepared to fight Karna to the death, but Krishna suggested that Ghatotkacha (Bhima's son) confront Karna instead.
Ghatotkacha, a rakshasa who was more powerful at night and skilled in illusions, fought Karna fiercely.
Unable to withstand Ghatotkacha's attacks, Karna used the divine weapon Indra's spear to kill Ghatotkacha.
The Pandava army mourned Ghatotkacha's death, but Krishna was pleased because Karna had used his one-time Indra's spear, which he had been saving for Arjuna.
During the late-night battle, both armies grew weary, and Arjuna proposed a temporary ceasefire for rest.
On the fifth day, Drona killed King Drupada and King Virata in battle.
Seeing Drona slaughtering the Pandava army, Krishna advised Arjuna to use deceit by spreading false news of Ashwatthama's death.
Arjuna opposed the deceit, but others, including a reluctant Yudhishthira, agreed.
Bhima killed an elephant named Ashwatthama and shouted that Ashwatthama was dead, causing Drona to doubt and ask the truth from Yudhishthira.
Under Krishna's urging, Yudhishthira lied to Drona, saying Ashwatthama was dead, leading Drona to lose his will to live.
Drona, in despair, sat in meditation, and Dhrishtadyumna took the opportunity to behead him, despite protests from warriors on both sides.
After Drona's death, the Kaurava army fled in disarray.
Ashwatthama, learning of his father's death, vowed revenge and used the Narayana weapon against the Pandava army.

relationships: Ashwatthama seeks revenge for Drona's death

extraction_text: Krishna, knowing the rules of the Narayana weapon, instructed the Pandava army to lay down their arms, saving them as the weapon does not harm those who surrender.
Ashwatthama then used the Agneya weapon, but Arjuna countered it with the Brahma weapon.
Sage Vyasa appeared, revealing that Krishna and Arjuna were incarnations of Narayana and Nara, Ashwatthama was an incarnation of Rudra, and all were blessed by Shiva, leading to a ceasefire.

relationships: Krishna and Arjuna as divine incarnations

extraction_text: Drona's father, Bharadvaja, saw the celestial nymph Hridika's body during a ritual, lost control of his passion, and his semen fell into a wooden bowl, from which Drona was born.
Drona studied Vedas and martial arts in the hermitage with Drupada, son of King Prishata, and they became close friends.
Drupada promised that when he inherited the kingdom, he would share his kingdom and wealth with Drona.
Drupada returned to inherit the kingship, and Drona married Kripi and had a son named Ashwatthama.
When Parashurama was distributing wealth to Brahmins, Drona arrived late and received all divine weapons instead.
Drona visited King Drupada, but Drupada rejected their friendship, citing their now unequal status and wealth.
Angered, Drona went to Hastinapura and became the martial arts teacher for the Kuru and Pandava princes.
Drona required all princes to promise to do something for him after completing their training.
Arjuna diligently served Drona and became his favorite student.
Ekalavya, a Nishada prince, sought to become Drona's student but was rejected due to his low caste.
Ekalavya made a clay statue of Drona, worshipped it as his teacher, and mastered archery on his own.
The Pandavas discovered Ekalavya's exceptional archery during a forest hunt.
Drona found Ekalavya and demanded his right thumb as tuition, which Ekalavya cut off and gave to him.

attributes.reason: To ensure no one surpassed Arjuna in archery

extraction_text: While bathing in the Ganges, a crocodile attacked Drona, and Arjuna quickly killed it with an arrow.
Drona rewarded Arjuna with the supreme divine weapon 'Brahmashira'.
After the Pandavas completed their training, Drona demanded they conquer Drupada's kingdom for him.
Drona returned half the kingdom to Drupada, stating they were now equals and could be friends again.
Drupada, filled with hatred, performed a sacrifice to obtain a son who could kill Drona, resulting in the birth of Dhrishtadyumna and Draupadi.
To protect his reputation, Drona accepted Dhrishtadyumna as his student and taught him martial arts.
As court martial arts teacher, Drona witnessed the power struggle between the Kauravas and Pandavas and was aware of Duryodhana's persecutions against the Pandavas.
Duryodhana's plot to burn the Pandavas in the lacquer house failed, and Arjuna won Draupadi for the Pandavas.

extraction_text: Duryodhana fought with Satyaki and was defeated.
Drona criticized Duryodhana for his past actions, including the dice game and insults toward the Pandavas and Draupadi.
When Jayadratha was in danger, Duryodhana went to Drona for help.
Drona stated that the war was the consequence of the dice game orchestrated by Shakuni, with Jayadratha as the stake.
Arjuna killed Jayadratha.
Duryodhana, in despair, complained that Drona favored Arjuna and neglected them.
Drona sorrowfully told Duryodhana that after Bhishma's fall, he knew the Kaurava victory was hopeless, and listed Duryodhana's errors.
On the fourth night, Duryodhana again complained that Drona favored the Pandavas and did not fight with full power.
Drona, both happy and angry, pointed out Arjuna's invincibility and harshly scolded Duryodhana for his cruel nature and causing innocent kings to die.
Drona fought fiercely against Arjuna, using all his divine weapons, which Arjuna countered effortlessly.
Drona felt joy seeing Arjuna's skill, considering it proof of his own excellence as a teacher.
Krishna devised a plan to make Yudhishthira falsely claim that Ashwatthama was dead.
Drona, trusting Yudhishthira, believed the lie and decided to lay down his weapons, practice yoga, and depart for heaven.
Dhrishtadyumna killed Drona, which is seen as the resolution of the feud between Drona and Drupada.
Heavenly sages called Drona, telling him his time on earth was over and to abandon weapons for the eternal path.
Drona laid down his weapons, practiced yoga, attained liberation, and his luminous form ascended to the Brahmaloka; Dhrishtadyumna only killed his physical body.

According to the Mahabharata's Adi Parva, the Bharata war was actually a war between gods and demons, with most Kaurava warriors being reincarnated Asuras and most Pandava warriors being incarnations of gods.
Bhishma, Drona, and Kripa, though fighting for the Kauravas, were incarnations of gods: Bhishma was Vasu, Drona was Brihaspati, and Kripa was Rudra.

attributes.relationships: All were teachers in the Kaurava court but divine incarnations

extraction_text: During the Pandavas' forest exile, Karna urged Duryodhana to go to the forest to insult them.
Indra disguised as a Brahmin begged Karna for his divine earrings and armor, which made him invincible; Surya warned Karna in a dream.
Karna gave his earrings and armor to Indra, upholding his vow to never refuse a Brahmin, and received the infallible Shakti spear in return, but with a limitation.
During the Kurukshetra War, Karna used the Shakti spear prematurely against Ghatotkacha, wasting it before his duel with Arjuna.
Krishna (Krishna) visited the Kaurava clan before the Mahabharata war, but Duryodhana refused reconciliation.
Krishna privately met Karna, revealing his birth secret as the eldest son of Kunti and the Pandavas, and urged him to join the Pandavas as king and husband of Draupadi.
Karna declined Krishna's offer, citing loyalty to his adoptive parents (the charioteer Adhiratha and his wife Radha) and gratitude to Duryodhana for his 13-year kingship.
Karna apologized for past harsh words against the Pandavas, wished Yudhishthira to be king, and requested secrecy about their conversation.
After hearing of the failed peace talks, Kunti went to the Ganges riverbank to meet Karna, confirmed his birth truth, and begged him to reunite with the Pandavas.
Karna refused Kunti, fearing ridicule from Kshatriya warriors, but promised to fight only Arjuna in the war so Kunti would retain five sons regardless of outcome.
Duryodhana requested Bhishma to lead the Kaurava army, and Bhishma agreed on condition of not fighting alongside Karna, which Karna accepted.
Bhishma and Drona belittled Karna as a 'half-warrior' before the war, angering Karna who vowed not to fight while Bhishma commanded.
After Bhishma fell on the battlefield, Karna visited him, sought forgiveness, and requested permission to join the fight.
Bhishma revealed he knew Karna was Kunti's son, explained his harshness was to prevent family division, and urged Karna to reunite with the Pandavas.
Karna reiterated his loyalty to Duryodhana and adoptive parents, refusing Bhishma's advice.
After Bhishma's fall, Karna recommended Drona as the next Kaurava commander despite Drona's prejudice against him.
During Drona's command, Karna fought bravely and used his divine 'Shakti' spear prematurely against Ghatotkacha, depleting his weapon meant for Arjuna.
After Drona's death, Karna became the Kaurava commander and was ultimately killed by his half-brother Arjuna.
Karna's lifelong suffering stemmed from his identity as a 'charioteer's son'.
Karna was born as a Kshatriya warrior but lived as 'son of a charioteer' in society, suffering humiliation and setbacks.

extraction_text: 然后，坚战向甘陀利请罪。甘陀利从蒙眼的布条中瞥见坚战的脚指头，顿时，她的愤怒的眼光使坚战的脚指甲变形。般度之子们赶紧后退，而此时，甘陀利的愤怒已经平息。

extraction_text: All survivors travel to the Ganges River to perform the water offering ceremony (tarpaṇa) for the fallen warriors.
Kunti, overcome with grief, reveals to the Pāṇḍavas that Karṇa was their eldest brother and requests they perform the water offering for him as well.

attributes.action: Revelation of family secret, request for rites
attributes.relationship_change: Pāṇḍavas learn Karṇa was their brother

extraction_text: The Pāṇḍavas, in great distress, perform the water offering ceremony for Karṇa as requested by their mother.
Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Gāndhārī, having lost their one hundred sons led by Duryodhana, remain filled with grief and anger despite Kṛṣṇa's earlier consolation.
Gāndhārī, using her divine sight, describes the horrific scenes of wives and mothers mourning their slain husbands and sons on the battlefield.
In this atmosphere of profound tragedy, Gāndhārī angrily pronounces a terrible curse upon Kṛṣṇa.
Kṛṣṇa accepts the curse but clarifies to Gāndhārī that the responsibility for the war's devastation lies with Duryodhana and that she, as his mother, also bears some fault.
Gāndhārī, hearing Kṛṣṇa's words, falls silent, her eyes filled with sorrow, seemingly feeling a sense of remorse.
The war and funeral rites conclude, but the psychological trauma and wounds inflicted by the conflict are destined to endure.
